Integration lifecycle
orig_caption: An architect is accountable for the whole arc, not only the design phase.
texts: Yellow phases are where integrations most often fail: unclear discovery on the left, missing operations on the right.

title: Integration journey with approval gates
orig_caption: Four gates. Each has criteria, an owner and an evidence list. Skipping a gate does not save time; it moves the discovery to production.
texts: A gate is a decision, not a meeting: it passes only when its criteria are evidenced, and failures are recorded as risks with owners.

title: From answers to architecture
orig_caption: Constraints come first and rule options out. Only then do you choose a pattern family, and only after that a delivery vehicle. Unknowns are carried forward as risks, never silently assumed.

title: SaaS to SaaS via cloud iPaaS
orig_caption: Everything is reachable over the internet. A cloud iPaaS or serverless glue is usually the fastest answer.

title: On-prem to SaaS via agent
orig_caption: The agent opens the connection outward. No inbound firewall rule is required, which is why security teams approve it fastest.

title: Hybrid with private connectivity
orig_caption: A private link joins the data centre to a cloud network; PaaS services are reached through private endpoints, never the public internet.

title: Multi-cloud with an event backbone
orig_caption: An event backbone (a Kafka platform or an event mesh) decouples clouds and sites from each other and from the data platform.

title: Mainframe offload
orig_caption: Leave the core system alone. Take messages from MQ, or capture changes from its database log, and publish them outward.

title: Partner connectivity via DMZ
orig_caption: Partners enter through a hardened DMZ component; nothing from the internet touches internal systems directly.

title: Edge and IoT
orig_caption: Sites must keep running when the WAN drops. Local brokers buffer and forward when the link returns.

title: Pattern family decision tree

title: Failure-injection test harness
orig_caption: Run the real integration against a mock API behind a fault proxy, a real Kafka and a real database in containers, then assert the end state.

orig_caption: Build once, promote the same artifact through environments, and approve with evidence.

title: Kafka architecture: producers, brokers with partitions, consumer groups
orig_caption: Topics are split into partitions; partitions are replicated across brokers; consumer groups share partitions.
texts: Writes and reads go to the partition leader; followers replicate
each partition: one consumer per group
A partition is an append-only log: [0][1][2][3][4]...  Each record has an offset. Consumers track their own position.
Records are retained for a time or size limit, or compacted to the latest value per key. Reading does not delete.

title: Retry topics and dead letter queue flow
orig_caption: Non-blocking retries: a failed record moves to a delay topic so the main partition keeps flowing. Trade-off: ordering for that key is no longer guaranteed.
